content:
Creating this topic to aggregate discussion around compilation from ArkLib whether via the native compiler or custom compiler(s), as well as the verification of such compilers.

cc: @Bas Spitters @Ryan Kim @Tobias Grosser and others.

As I mentioned, I have an MLIR-inspired compiler for CT crypto similar to jasmin. I hope we can base it on VeIR.
I aligned my port of our https://github.com/AU-COBRA/AUCurves library to the dialect used by fractionalize, which were a bit more developed than the ones I came up with myself. Thanks again for the nice work @Ryan Kim
I think the easiest way to target it would be via Hax, but there are other possibilities too.

@Bas Spitters Just to clarify, do you mean you ported AUCurves to match https://github.com/fractalyze/prime-ir? Also, what exactly do you mean by targeting it via Hax? Does it mean Plonky3 will be extracted into Lean through Hax, and then become executable via an MLIR dialect built on top of VeIR? Did I understand that correctly?
